correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated all 11776 faces (including empty), f-cardinality vector (1,27,270,1278,3078,3834,2412,756,108,12), and maximal-facet profile 54 of size five, 324 of size seven and 12 of size nine. Independent 5867-pair vertex-pivot matching leaves one 0-cell, one 3-cell and 39 4-cells; topological sort checked acyclicity across all 56619 covering incidences. Exact integer Morse projection recurrence yielded boundary coefficients −1 seven times, 0 twenty-three times, +1 nine times. Gcd one makes the 4-to-3 boundary primitive, so CW elementary changes cancel one 3/4-cell pair leaving ∨38 S⁴. A mod-two homology rank would not alone prove this integral wedge; the integer primitive differential does.

originality.rationale: A material priority clarification is essential: Falcón 2011 Table 2 already reports every positive face count (27,270,1278,3078,3834,2412,756,108,12), total 11775. Thus that exact enumeration is NOT new. Hämäläinen 2009 computes a trade-intersection space for a fixed Latin square, not the complex of all partial Latin squares. The surviving novelty and value are the integral Morse attaching degrees and 38-sphere homotopy classification; no covering theorem was found in primary text or indexed Hamming-graph records.

value.rationale: Partial Latin squares form a foundational natural space in combinatorics, and the all-partial-square containment complex is a canonical independence complex of H(3,3). Determining its complete integral homotopy type—not merely known face counts—is a concrete useful finite invariant and a benchmark for higher-order Latin-square topology.

final_claim: For the canonical complex of all labelled order-three partial Latin squares (Ind(H(3,3))), the integral homotopy type is a wedge of exactly 38 four-spheres, via an explicit integral acyclic Morse reduction.
limitations: Only order-three labelled partial Latin squares; no all-n theorem.
The f-vector is expressly prior work (Falcón 2011 Table 2); only homotopy/Morse integral classification assessed as new.
